To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a cooperative with several member-supplied products can use either the linear programming model or the pooling constraint method to calculate returns for all products.

the returns to be allocated to each member-supplied commodity can be calculated using a linear programming model or the pooling constraint method, and that the linear programming model can be used when the assumptions underlying it are valid, while the pooling constraint method can be employed in the case of multiple product marketing cooperatives that are subject to the assumptions underlying the linear programming model.
the shadow prices of a linear program are the correct values to be assigned to each member's product as returns to be paid for his product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and realistic method of calculating the returns to be allocated to each product handled by a cooperative.
the problem of computing the shadow prices (or returns) for a marketing cooperative handling several products.
the determination of shadow prices as member returns for a multiple product cooperative.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pooling constraint method is more general than the linear programming method, but the linear programming model is easier to use.
the pooling constraint method is the more general and flexible method of determining returns for a marketing cooperative with several member-supplied products.
the "pooling" constraint method of deriving shadow prices is a useful tool for the marketing cooperative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to determine shadow prices as member returns for a cooperative that handles several types or grades or member-supplied products.
the linear programming model is useful in the multiple product case when the assumptions of the model are satisfied.

the pooling constraint method is the most general of the two methods presented and can be used to solve the multiple product problem for any type of marketing cooperative, including those that have a single homogeneous product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a marketing cooperative can simultaneously determine returns to be allotted to each member-supplied commodity by solving a single linear programming problem.
the pooling constraint method can be used to solve the multiple product cooperative return problem.

the pooling constraint method provides a general approach for computing member returns when there are more than one member product and/or when the cooperative has more than one buyer for each member product.
